title: Madrid & Barcelona.

days.title: Arrival in Madrid
days.desc: Touch down in Madrid, the vibrant heart of Spain, known for its rich history and lively atmosphere, and transfer privately to your hotel. Overnight in Madrid.

days.title: Madrid
days.desc: A 3-hour guided tour takes in Madrid's highlights — Puerta del Sol, Gran Vía, the regal Royal Palace (entrance not included) and the lively Plaza Mayor. Overnight in Madrid.
days.taste: A stop for churros con chocolate at one of Madrid's historic chocolaterías, a Madrileño breakfast tradition since the 19th century.

days.title: Madrid — Toledo Excursion
days.desc: A guided 5-hour exploration of Toledo, a UNESCO World Heritage city, uncovering its historical charm through enchanting streets and architectural wonders. Return to Madrid for the evening. Overnight in Madrid.
days.experience: Toledo's Alcázar and its winding medieval streets reflect centuries of coexistence between Christian, Muslim and Jewish communities — look for the Sinagoga del Tránsito and the Mezquita del Cristo de la Luz along the way.

days.title: Madrid to Barcelona
days.desc: A scenic coach transfer to Barcelona, the “City of Counts”, renowned for Antoni Gaudí's architecture, Catalan culture and the iconic Sagrada Família. Overnight in Barcelona.

days.title: Barcelona
days.desc: A 3-hour guided tour roams the historic Gothic Quarter, strolls down La Rambla, and takes in Gaudí's Casa Batlló and Casa Milà. Overnight in Barcelona.
days.shopping: Passeig de Gràcia, right by Casa Batlló, is Barcelona's flagship shopping avenue for both international brands and Catalan designers.

days.title: Barcelona — Montserrat Excursion
days.desc: A guided 5-hour journey to Montserrat, a mystical mountain retreat, visiting the Montserrat Monastery, home to the revered Black Madonna. Overnight in Barcelona.
days.experience: The Montserrat funicular or cable car ride up the mountain is part of the experience — jagged rock formations rise around the monastery on all sides.

days.title: Depart Barcelona
days.desc: A private transfer takes you from your Barcelona hotel to the airport, concluding your journey through Madrid and Barcelona.

about.title: Best season
about.body: April–June and September–October for mild temperatures in both cities; July–August is hot, especially in Madrid, which sits inland on Spain's central plateau.

about.title: Weather
about.body: Madrid: continental, hot dry summers up to 35°C and cold winters. Barcelona: Mediterranean, milder year-round thanks to the coast, rarely dropping below 5°C in winter.

about.title: Currency & docs
about.body: The Euro (€) is the local currency, and Spain is a Schengen Area member — no separate visa is needed for Schengen visa holders.

goodToKnow.title: Sagrada Família
goodToKnow.body: Entry is not included in the Barcelona city tour — book Sagrada Família tickets in advance, as timed-entry slots often sell out days ahead in peak season.

goodToKnow.title: Siesta hours
goodToKnow.body: Many smaller shops in both cities close for a few hours in early afternoon — plan independent shopping around this local rhythm.

goodToKnow.title: What to pack
goodToKnow.body: Comfortable shoes for cobbled old-town streets in both cities; sun protection for Madrid's intense summer sun.

goodToKnow.title: Tipping
goodToKnow.body: Tipping is modest in Spain — rounding up or leaving 5–10% for good restaurant service is generous rather than expected.
